Not great at any of this, but I'd like to contribute more so I'll take a look at fixing this for about the next 2 hours

I'm still trying to get things to build on my machine. I knew getting Windows would be a pain but they're just so much cheaper and still easier to use for me than Linux.

Anyway, I haven't really found the problem, but I have found a couple of ways I think I could fix it. For one if I just added a check [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/angular2/src/router/router_outlet.ts#L83) and bound to null if there where no param this would go away, but it might not be the most elegant approach.

I think I found it. That was a bit more than the 2 hours I said, but hay at least now I understand how routing in angular works much better. Only problem is that while I can now get it to compile the tests won't run. Gah. Anyway the problem is I believe on this [line](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/angular2/src/router/route_registry.ts#L215). `params` should  be internalized to `{}` I think it might also make sense to add a check to the constructor for RouteParams to see if the params it gets passed are null and then either silently deal with it or throw an exception. Probably the later, because then tests would have failed and this would have been found much earlier.

issue.body:
I decided to try to fix [this](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/3755#issuecomment-133613666). It took me a lot longer than originally expected, but I think I've done it. The root cause seems to have been a Router.generate was changed apparently in this [commit](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/f66ce096d8d908fcc0a643a14412136e74025c3d) to allow the deep linking from anywhere. It also changed the method from essentially just passing arguments on to the relevant component's RouteRecognizer to generate the arguments from just a list. When this was done it should have always passed at least an empty StringMap for params, but because params is initialized to null this was not the case. 

I had a bit of trouble testing as the testing scripts are not designed to run on windows, but `./node_modules/.bin/protractor protractor-js.conf.js` runs fine with my edits, but throws an exception if I remove just my edits to route_registry.ts.

`./node_modules/.bin/gulp test.js --browsers=${KARMA_BROWSERS:-ChromeCanary}` seems to run fine in either case.

body: If you guys want to use this in the current version you can probably check if routeParams.params is null.
